rules.instruction: When the description states that when a check finds a condition not met, a task is performed to correct the item, and the process then goes back to repeat that same check before continuing: Model the check as an exclusive gateway with one branch to the correction task and one branch onward to the next step. Connect the correction task's outgoing flow back into an exclusive gateway (merge) placed before the check, so that the check is repeated. Do not connect the correction task directly to the next step, do not omit the merge, and do not add a parallel gateway to this loop.
rules.situation: the description lists several prerequisites that must all be satisfied before a decision, and a prerequisite that is not met can be remedied by the applicant obtaining or renewing the required item

rules.instruction: When the description lists several separate requirements that an applicant must provide or prove, and it states that checking them has a fulfilled outcome and a not-fulfilled outcome with a named remedial step: Model each listed requirement as its own task in the order the description gives: a user task where the applicant must prepare or obtain the item, and a service task where the description states an automated check. Do not wrap these tasks in an embedded subprocess. After the last check, place an exclusive gateway with one branch for the fulfilled outcome and one for the not-fulfilled outcome. On the not-fulfilled branch, model the remedial action the description names as its own manual or user task, then route back to the check. Keep every listed requirement and every named remedial action as a separate element, and keep any gateway the description implies before the first check or after the verification.
rules.situation: the description lists several separate requirements that an applicant must provide or prove, and it states that checking them has a fulfilled outcome and a not-fulfilled outcome with a named remedial step

rules.instruction: When the description states that a participant's document must meet validity or eligibility conditions (such as a minimum remaining validity period, an issue-date limit, or a required number of blank pages) before an application can be accepted: Model a separate user task, performed by the participant or the reviewing party, that checks the document against the stated conditions. Place this check before the exclusive gateway that decides whether the application can proceed. If the check fails, model a separate task in which the participant obtains a replacement document, and connect that task back into a merge gateway placed before the check so the check is repeated. Do not fold the document check into the decision gateway or into a generic preparation task.

rules.instruction: When the description names an activity or outcome in a short phrase, and a generated task or event label adds qualifiers such as the time period, the recipient, or a status that the description does not use as the activity's name: Label the task or event with the core verb-object action or outcome that the description names, and omit added qualifiers (periods, recipients, statuses) unless the description uses them as part of the activity's name.
